Final theorems: (1) Theorem 2.1 — for K/F finite, k ≥ 1 and every q, H^q_ét(M^ϖ_{n,K}, O_L/p^k) is a profinite O_L-module whose Pontryagin dual is a smooth finitely presented representation of G′ — together with the machinery its proof needs: the equivariant semi-stable formal model of M^ϖ_n with finitely many G-orbits of irreducible components, each with open stabiliser (Proposition 2.6); the Bloch–Kato–Hyodo filtration on mod p nearby cycles extended to formal schemes, with its graded pieces Ω^q_log, Ω^{q-1}/B, Ω^{q-1}/Z and the vanishing above pe/(p−1) (Theorem 2.4, and Remark 2.5 for q = 1); and the pro-object formalism of cohomologically profinite, G′-continuous and cpcf sheaves with its two-out-of-three lemma (§2.1.3, Lemmas 2.9 and 2.10). (2) Theorem 2.14 — for F ≠ Q_p and n ≥ 1 the mod p^k multiplicity spaces Π_M(V^+_k) are not admissible whenever Π_M(V) ≠ 0 — with Nakajima's theorem supplying the non-vacuity, and the mechanism: an admissible finitely presented representation is, up to finite O_L-modules, a parabolic induction, so it admits no map from the universal completion of a supercuspidal representation (Proposition 2.18). (3) The comparison of the arithmetic and geometric cohomologies: the completed cohomology H^1_ét(M^p_{n,Q̄_p}, L(1)) of the tower of coefficient fields, the theorem that it is the almost-smooth part of H^{1,+}_{C_p} (Proposition 5.16) with its corollaries, and the finite length of (H^{1,+}_{Q̄_p}/p^k)^{Gal_K} (Proposition 5.19). Record as open: whether H^{1,+}_{Q̄_p} is dense in H^{1,+}_{C_p} (Question 5.18), whether H^1_ét(M^ϖ_{n,C_p},k_L) is profinite, and the missing Poincaré duality for such analytic spaces, which would make Theorem 2.1 a statement about compactly supported cohomology where Berkovich's smoothness of the G-action is available. Import the log structures from CrystallineCohomology CR.5, the formal-model nearby cycles from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1, and the mod p representation theory of G′ from the roadmap proposed above; do not plan the p-adic local Langlands correspondence here.

routes.title: P-adic local Langlands for GL₂(Q_p), Part II: the geometric realisation in the Drinfeld tower
routes.reason: This is the Part II proposed by PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20-B for the geometric realisation of the correspondence in the Drinfeld tower, and the present paper completes it: where the first paper computed the multiplicity of one irreducible representation, this one determines the whole cohomology as a Gal_{Q_p} × G × Ǧ-module, in an Emerton-style factorisation over the blocks of the mod p representation theory and the Kisin rings of the types. That is new layers in the direction of the same parent — R30.5 already owns the blocks and projective envelopes and R30.3 the correspondence — and no stage of the parent mentions the tower.
routes.brief: Added to the brief already proposed by PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20-B. Final theorem (Theorem 5.15 = Theorem 0.1): for L large enough, H^1_ét(M^p_{n,Q̄_p}, L(1)) ≅ ⊕_M (⊕̂_B Π^*(ρ_{B,M}) ⊗ ρ_{B,M} ⊗ Ř_{B,M}) ⊗_L JL(M), the first sum over the types M of level ≤ n, the completed sum over the blocks B of the mod p category, the tensor products over the Kisin ring R_{B,M}. Plan the three layers it decomposes into. (1) The individual multiplicities: Theorem 5.1, the multiplicity of an absolutely irreducible V of dimension ≤ 2 (including the characters, which live in the special types and come by twisting from the Drinfeld half-plane); Theorem 5.8, the multiplicity Hom_G(Π^*, H^1_ét) = V_{M,L} ⊗ JL(M) of an absolutely irreducible unitary Banach representation, proved from the fundamental diagram together with the computation of Hom_G(Π^*, Ω^1) (Proposition 5.7); and Theorem 5.9, the vanishing for V of dimension ≥ 3, which the mod p finiteness theorem makes natural. Add the functional analysis these need: G-bounded vectors, universal unitary completions and the identification of the étale inside the pro-étale cohomology (Lemma 5.3, Proposition 5.6). (2) The families: the Kisin ring R_{B,M} of the representations of type M in a block, its structure as a finite product of principal ideal rings of bounded analytic functions on an open subset of P^1 with its universal representation ρ_{B,M} (Theorem 5.11), the rigidity lemma that makes such a representation unique (Lemma 5.12), and the interpolated G-representation Π^*(ρ_{B,M}) with its three equivalent descriptions (Definition 5.13). (3) The decomposition: the block decomposition of the integral cohomology, the multiplicity modules m_{B,M} = Hom_{G×Ǧ}(P_B ⊗ JL(M), H^1_ét(M^p_{n,Q̄_p})) with their independence of n and their central character (Remark 5.21), and Theorem 5.22 — that R^{ps,δ_M}_B acts through R_{B,M} and that m_{B,M} ≅ m^{δ_M}_B(Π^*(ρ_{B,M})) ⊗ ρ_{B,M} ⊗ Ř_{B,M} — which interpolates Theorem 5.8 over the closed points. Import the blocks, projective envelopes and R = T from R30.5/R30.6, the Kisin rings from LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3, the mod p finiteness from the two roadmaps proposed above, and the geometry of the tower from the pro-étale roadmap. Record the hypothesis p > 3 as a hypothesis (it enters through the global arguments and Paškūnas–Tung; for p = 3 the statement survives except possibly for the blocks containing a twist of the Steinberg), and record as an expectation, not a target, that the quotient of the geometric by the arithmetic cohomology may be arithmetically meaningless.

routes.reason: This paper is a heavy consumer of the parent roadmap of the Part II below: R30.2 for the categories of smooth mod p, admissible Banach and locally analytic representations and the mod p classification, R30.3 for Colmez's functor and the correspondence V ↦ Π(V), R30.5 for the blocks, the projective envelopes P_π and the deformation rings, and R30.6 for the precise Paškūnas, Hu–Tan and Tung statements. It is in turn a good source for the exact forms it needs and which those stages must export: the R = T theorem in the shape ι^δ_B(T^δ_B(g)) = g + δε(g)g^{-1} in End(V(π)) with its p ≥ 5, p = 3 and p = 2 cases (Theorem 1.15); the rationality bookkeeping relating blocks over k_L to Galois orbits of blocks over F̄_p (Remarks 1.11–1.13); and the statement that every π in a block occurs in the finite-length module cut out of a space of automorphic forms (Proposition 4.10).

R08.3 constructs Kisin's potentially semi-stable deformation rings with fixed Hodge and inertial type and characterises their characteristic-zero points. The ring R_{B,M} of §5.2 is the refinement this paper needs: the type is fixed as a whole Weil–Deligne representation M rather than as a Galois type, the ring is cut out of a pseudo-character deformation ring, and it is proved to be a finite product of principal ideal rings isomorphic to bounded analytic functions on an open subset of P^1 (Theorem 5.11) — which is what makes a pointwise decomposition interpolate.

R31.4 owns p-adic local–global compatibility and R31.5 the patched completed modules with their support and multiplicity statements. §4.1 consumes precisely those, for the Shimura curves of a quaternion algebra over a totally real field: Paškūnas's identification S^1(S_{ψ,λ,m}) ≅ Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ,m} of Scholze's functor with completed cohomology (Proposition 4.13) and the isotypy statement ρ_m ⊗ N ≅ Ĥ^1_{ψ,λ}(U^p,O_L)_m (Proposition 4.14). The paper is a good source for the shape in which these have to be exported to answer a purely local question.

R18.3 (‘Definite quaternionic forms’) defines algebraic modular forms on a definite quaternion algebra with their Hecke operators. §4.1.3 needs exactly that, together with the Galois-to-Hecke dictionary sending T_v to tr(ρ̄(Frob_v)) and S_v to N(v)^{-1}det(ρ̄(Frob_v)) and the resulting maximal ideal m.

R16.3 is local Langlands for GL_2, R17.1 the quaternionic local transfer and R17.3 the global Jacquet–Langlands correspondence. §4.1.2 builds its two quaternion algebras by interchanging the invariants at one place above p and one infinite place, and moves between them; the paper is a good source for that construction and for the auxiliary place that makes the tame level small enough.

R06.3 attaches a potentially semi-stable Weil–Deligne parameter to a de Rham representation (Fontaine's recipe). The paper needs it for (φ,N,Gal_F)-modules of rank 2 and in the packaged form M ↦ (WD(M), LL(M), JL(M)), with the notions of supercuspidal (WD irreducible of slope 1/2), special (N ≠ 0, slopes 0 and 1) and of level ≤ n.

R07.5 (‘Local residual types and Serre weights’) owns Serre weights. What this paper needs on top is the Barthel–Livné package for the compact inductions they generate: End_G I(σ) ≅ F̄_p[T] with I(σ) free over it, and the rigidity statement that every proper quotient of I(σ) has finite length.

H1 builds formal models, specialisation and the nearby-cycle formalism with the tube stalk formula. §2.1.1 needs the formal-scheme version: the canonical log structure of a semi-stable formal scheme in Berkovich's sense, the sheaves R^iΨ Z/p^n(j) on the special fibre as derived functors of Berkovich's nearby-cycle functor, and the Kummer symbol maps i^*(M^gp)^{⊗q} → R^qΨ Z/p^n(q) that carry the Bloch–Kato–Hyodo filtration. The paper is a good source for all of it, and its Theorem 2.4 is the statement H1 would have to export for a non-quasi-compact model.

ET.6a constructs the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers with their actions and period morphisms and proves the infinite-level moduli description and duality isomorphism. This paper needs, beyond that, the descent of M^ϖ_n to F with its G′-action — which is what makes the arithmetic cohomology H^•_ét(M^ϖ_{n,K}, −) over a finite K the object of study — and the Stein affinoid perfectoid cover of the infinite level with its Mittag-Leffler property (Lemma 3.3).

gaps.detail: Four inputs were unpublished when the paper appeared and must not be treated as available: [19] (Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł, ‘Correspondance de Langlands locale p-adique et anneaux de Kisin’, Acta Arith., ‘à paraître’) supplies the prodiscrete module Y_B with its Corollary 3.12 and the fact that J kills Y_B, both used in the proof of Theorem 5.24 (i); [25] (Dospinescu–Paškūnas–Schraen, ‘à paraître’, since published in J. reine angew. Math.) supplies the globalisation and several lemmas of §4.1; [42] (Hu–Wang, arXiv:2201.01464) is cited in Remark 4.4 for finer results on S^1(I(χ_1,χ_2)); [26] (Dotto–Emerton–Gee, arXiv:2207.04671) is cited for an alternative argument in §1.4. A design job should plan the statements actually used, not the papers.

The factorisation is proved for p > 3. Footnote 2 (p. 2) says the hypothesis is used in some global arguments and to quote [53] directly, and that it is ‘sans doute superflue’; for p = 3 the statement of Theorem 0.1 remains correct except possibly for the contribution of the blocks containing a twist of the Steinberg, and p = 2 is excluded throughout (the finiteness theorem of chapter 4 assumes p > 2). Removing the hypothesis is open and may not be planned as a target.

The paper obtains the integral block decomposition H^{1,+}_{Q̄_p} ≅ ⊕̂_B [P_B ⊗_{E_B} 𝕞_B(H^{1,+}_{Q̄_p})] (§5.3.2) but says explicitly that it does not seem easy to describe the integral module 𝕞_B(H^{1,+}_{Q̄_p}); only its generic fibre is computed, in Theorem 5.24. An integral form of the factorisation is not available.

Several statements in the paper are expectations, not results: Question 5.18 asks whether H^{1,+}_{Q̄_p} is dense in H^{1,+}_{C_p}; Remark 0.6 (i) observes that a Poincaré duality for the tower — not available — would give the first part of Theorem 0.5 for all q; Remark 2.3 expects the finite-presentation statement to hold in arbitrary dimension; Remark 4.29 expects Theorem 4.26 to hold for F ≠ Q_p although Theorem 4.1 does not; Remark 1.18 records Emerton's conjecture that an admissible proper quotient of I(σ) is of finite length for general F. The introduction also suggests that the quotient of the cohomology of M^p_{n,C_p} by that of M^p_{n,Q̄_p} may be arithmetically meaningless ‘bruit’, to which the authors ‘ont échoué à lui trouver une interprétation’.

Theorem 1.21 (finite length is detected by the cosocle) and Theorem 1.24 are proved only for F = Q_p because they use the full Barthel–Livné–Breuil classification of the smooth irreducible mod p representations, which is unknown for F ≠ Q_p; the same gap is why the finite-length Theorem 4.1 is specific to Q_p while the finite-presentation Theorem 2.1 holds for all F. The classification for F ≠ Q_p may not be planned.

The factorisation produces, for each type M, the G-representation Π^*(ρ_{B,M}) interpolating the duals Π(ρ_x)^* and the Ǧ-representation JL(M), but the paper constructs no functor realising a p-adic Jacquet–Langlands correspondence; that remains a programme (as in Remark 0.3 of the companion paper). A roadmap may plan the objects appearing in Theorem 5.15 but not a correspondence.
